title: Short Stuff: Black Cowboys
summary: Short Stuff episode on black cowboys in the American West. The hosts say many post-Civil War cowboys were Black and that the job was open to enslaved people, while white workers avoided the "cowboy" label until it gained cachet back East. They credit Larry Kelly of the Black Cowboy Museum in Rosenberg, Texas, and note the Civil War created labor demand that fell to African American workers. They profile Bass Reeves (first African American U.S. Marshal west of the Mississippi, possibly a model for the Lone Ranger), Bose Ikard (right-hand man to Charles Goodnight, basis for Joshua Deats in Lonesome Dove), Bill Pickett (rodeo pioneer who invented bulldogging/steer wrestling), Isom Dart (horse thief shot by Tom Horn), and Nat Love (Deadwood Dick, whose 1907 autobiography is discussed). Segment on Blazing Saddles and The Lone Ranger movie is light commentary.

segments.title: Opening banter and Blazing Saddles
segments.summary: Hosts open the episode, joke about Dave Kustan, and mention Blazing Saddles' fictional Black cowboy Sheriff Bart while saying many real Black cowboys were left out of Western media.

segments.title: Black cowboys after the Civil War and the origin of the term cowboy
segments.summary: Hosts say many post-Civil War cowboys were Black and that the job was open to enslaved people. They describe white workers avoiding the label until it became cool back East. They credit Larry Kelly of the Black Cowboy Museum, note the word cowboy versus cow hand question, and say they could not corroborate the etymology elsewhere.

segments.title: Southern migration to Texas and the Civil War's effect on cowboy work
segments.summary: Cowboy life grew out of Southern white migration to Texas for cheap land, with enslaved people brought along. During the Civil War, enslaved Black workers kept ranches and herds running; afterward, labor demand for cattle herding remained high.

segments.title: Famous Black cowboys: Bass Reeves, Bose Ikard, Bill Pickett, Isom Dart
segments.summary: Profiles of Bass Reeves, a U.S. Marshal who may have inspired the Lone Ranger; Bose Ikard, Charles Goodnight's right-hand man and basis for a Lonesome Dove character; Bill Pickett, who invented bulldogging and faced segregated rodeos; and Isom Dart, a horse thief shot by Tom Horn.

segments.title: Nat Love and his autobiography
segments.summary: Nat Love, known as Deadwood Dick, is described as the most famous Black cowboy. The hosts discuss his name spelling and the full title of his 1907 autobiography, and note his account departs from fact in places.
topics: Life and Adventures of Nat Love

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts recommend reading Nat Love's autobiography, mention the show's production credit, and end the episode.
